<h>Lectio 3</h>
De Expositióne S. Basilíi Epíscopi in Isaíam Prophétam
<r>In cap. 8 post initium</r>
<c>A</c>ccéssi, inquit, ad prophetíssam, et in útero accépit et péperit fílium. Quod María prophetíssa fúerit, ad quam próxime accéssit Isaías per prænotiónem spíritus, nemo contradíxerit, qui sit memor verbórum Maríæ, quæ prophético affláta spíritu elocúta est. Quid enim ait? Magníficat ánima mea Dóminum: et exsultávit spíritus meus in Deo, salutári meo. Quia respéxit humilitátem ancíllæ suæ: ecce enim ex hoc beátam me dicent omnes generatiónes. Quod si ánimum accommodáveris univérsis eius verbis, non útique per dissídium negáveris eam fuísse prophetíssam, quod Dómini Spíritus in eam supervénerit, et virtus Altíssimi obumbráverit ei.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.

<r>℟.</r> Virgo parens Christi, paritúra Deum genuísti: fúlgida stella maris, nos prótege, nos tueáris:
* Dum paris, et gaudes, Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.
<r>℣.</r> Intercéde pia pro nobis Virgo María.
<r>℟.</r> Dum paris, et gaudes, Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Cantant cæli ágmina laudes.

<r>Te Deum</r>
<c>T</c>e Deum laudámus: * te Dóminum confitémur.

Tibi omnes Ángeli, * tibi Cæli, et univérsæ Potestátes:
Tibi Chérubim et Séraphim * incessábili voce proclámant:
<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus * Dóminus Deus Sábaoth.
Pleni sunt cæli et terra * maiestátis glóriæ tuæ.
Te gloriósus * Apostolórum chorus,
Te Prophetárum * laudábilis númerus,
Te Mártyrum candidátus * laudat exércitus.
Te per orbem terrárum * sancta confitétur Ecclésia,
Patrem * imménsæ maiestátis;

Sanctum quoque * Paráclitum Spíritum.

<n>(Fit reverentia)</n> Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.

<n>(Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus)</n> Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.

<h>Reading 3</h>
From the Commentary of St. Basil, Bishop, on the Prophet Isaias
<r>On chapter 8 near the beginning</r>
“I went to the prophetess”, he says, “and she conceived and bore a son.” To see Mary in the prophetess whom Isaias approached by spiritual foreknowledge one need only recall the words Mary uttered when she was inspired by the spirit of prophecy: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Saviour; because He has regarded the lowliness of His handmaid; for behold, henceforth all generation shall call me blessed.” In fact, if you bear in mind all that she said, you can only agree that she was indeed the prophetess, since the spirit of Lord came upon her, and the power of the Most High overshadowed her.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>S</c>exto Idus Novémbris Luna vicésima octáva. Anno Dómini 2026
<h>O</h>ctáva ómnium Sanctórum.
<h>R</h>omæ, via Lavicána, tértio ab Urbe milliário, pássio sanctórum Mártyrum Cláudii, Nicostráti, Symphoriáni, Castórii et Simplícii, qui, primo in cárcerem missi, deínde scorpiónibus gravíssime cæsi, tandem, cum ex fide Christi dimovéri non possent, a Diocletiáno iussi sunt in flúvium præcípites dari.
<h>I</h>bídem, via Lavicána, natális sanctórum Quátuor Coronatórum fratrum, id est Sevéri, Severiáni, Carpóphori et Victoríni; qui, sub eódem Imperatóre, íctibus plumbatárum usque ad mortem cæsi sunt. Horum autem nómina, quæ póstea, interiéctis annis, Dómino revelánte, osténsa sunt, cum mínime reperíri tunc potuíssent, statútum fuit ut anniversária dies ipsórum, una cum illis quinque, sub nómine sanctórum Quátuor Coronatórum recolerétur; qui mos, étiam postquam reveláta sunt, in Ecclésia perseverávit.
<h>I</h>tem Romæ sancti Deúsdedit Papæ Primi, qui tanti meriti fuit, ut leprósum ósculo a lepra sanáverit.
<h>I</h>n vico Blexen, ad Visúrgim flúvium, in Germánia, sancti Willehádi, qui primus éxstitit Breménsis civitátis Epíscopus; atque, una cum sancto Bonifátio, cuius discípulus fuit, in Frísia et Saxónia Evangélium propagávit.
<h>S</h>uessíone, in Gálliis, sancti Godefrídi, Ambianénsis Epíscopi, magnæ sanctitátis viri.
<h>A</h>pud Virodúnum, in Gállia, sancti Mauri, Epíscopi et Confessóris.
<h>T</h>urónis, in Gállia, sancti Clari Presbýteri, cuius sanctus Paulínus epitáphium scripsit.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.661b34bb62:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>N</c>ovember 8th 2026, the 28th day of the Moon,
<h>T</h>omorrow is the Octave of All Saints.
<h>U</h>pon the same 8th day of November, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, upon the Lavican Way, upon the third milestone from the city, the holy martyrs Claudius, Nicostratus, Symphorian, Castorius, and Simplicius, they were first cast into prison, then heavily lashed with loaded scourges, and as their faith in Christ could not be shaken the Emperor Diocletian commanded that they should be cast into the river.
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, upon the Lavican Way, the holy martyrs called the "Crowned" brethren, Severus, Severian, Carpophorus, and Victorinus, who under the aforesaid Emperor Diocletian were flogged to death with scourges loaded with lead. Their names were afterwards revealed by the Lord after diverse years, but as they were unknown at the time it was ordained that on the anniversary of their deaths they should be commemorated, along with the five above mentioned, under the title of the Four that were Crowned, and the said custom hath still gone on in the Church ever since their names have been known.
<h>A</h>t Rome, (in the year 618,) the holy Pope Deusdedit, whose grace was such that by his kiss he made a leper clean.
<h>A</h>t Bremen, (about the year 789,) holy Willehad, first Bishop of that see. He spread the Gospel in Friesland and Saxony along with holy Boniface, whose disciple he was.
<h>A</h>t Soissons, in Gaul, (in the year 1118,) holy Godfrey, Bishop of Amiens, a man of great holiness.
<h>A</h>t Verdun, the holy Confessor Maurus, Bishop (of that see.)
<h>A</h>t Tours, (in the fourth century,) the holy priest Clarus, whose epitaph was written by holy Paulinus.
